summary: The gid hanasheh (the sciatic nerve in the thigh) may not be eaten. This applies to farm animals and wild animals, but not to birds, since a bird has no "spoon" of the thigh.

chunks.he: גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה נוֹהֵג בָּאָרֶץ וּבְחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ,
chunks.en: The gid hanasheh applies in Eretz Yisrael and outside Eretz Yisrael,
chunks.explain: The gid hanasheh is a sinew in the back leg that we may not eat.
chunks.st: The prohibition of eating the sciatic nerve applies both in Eretz Yisrael and outside of Eretz Yisrael,

words.note: The gid hanasheh, the sciatic nerve.

chunks.en: when the Beis HaMikdash stands and when it does not,
chunks.st: in the presence of, i.e., the time of, the Temple and not in the presence of the Temple, and

chunks.en: with plain animals and with korbanos.
chunks.st: with regard to non-sacred animals and with regard to sacrificial animals.

chunks.en: And it applies to farm animals and wild animals,
chunks.st: And it applies to domesticated animals and to undomesticated animals,

chunks.he: בְּיָרֵךְ שֶׁל יָמִין וּבְיָרֵךְ שֶׁל שְׂמֹאל.
chunks.en: to the right thigh and to the left thigh.
chunks.st: to the thigh of the right leg and to the thigh of the left leg.

chunks.en: But it does not apply to a bird,
chunks.st: But it does not apply to a bird,

chunks.en: because it has no "spoon" of the thigh.
chunks.explain: The round part of the hip bone; the Torah mentions it.
chunks.st: due to the fact that the verse makes reference to the sciatic nerve as being “upon the spoon of the thigh” (Genesis 32:33), and a bird has no spoon of the thigh.

chunks.en: And it applies to an unborn calf.
chunks.st: And the prohibition applies to a late-term animal fetus [shalil] in the womb.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: It does not apply to an unborn calf,
chunks.st: It does not apply to a fetus;

chunks.en: and its forbidden fat is allowed.
chunks.st: and similarly, its fat is permitted.

words.note: Fat that is forbidden to eat.

chunks.he: וְאֵין הַטַּבָּחִין נֶאֱמָנִין עַל גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה,
chunks.en: And the butchers are not trusted about the gid hanasheh.
chunks.explain: To say that they took it out.
chunks.st: And butchers are not deemed credible to say that the sciatic nerve was removed;

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: And the Sages say:
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: They are trusted about it and about the cheilev.
chunks.st: They are deemed credible about the sciatic nerve and about the forbidden fat.

summary: We may send a thigh to a non-Jew with the gid hanasheh still in it, because it is easy to see. When taking out the gid hanasheh, we must take out all of it.

chunks.en: A person may send a thigh to a non-Jew
chunks.st: a Jewish person may send the thigh of an animal to a gentile

chunks.en: with the gid hanasheh inside it,
chunks.st: with the sciatic nerve in it,
chunks.stMore: without concern that the gentile will then sell the thigh to a Jew and the Jew will eat the sciatic nerve.

chunks.en: because its place is easy to see.
chunks.st: This leniency is due to the fact that the place of the sciatic nerve is conspicuous in the thigh.

chunks.en: Someone who takes out the gid hanasheh
chunks.st: One who removes the sciatic nerve

chunks.en: must take out all of it.
chunks.st: must scrape away the flesh in the area surrounding the nerve to ensure that he will remove all of it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: Just enough to keep the mitzvah of taking it out.
chunks.st: Scraping is not required; it is sufficient to excise it from the area above the rounded protrusion in order to thereby fulfill the mitzva of removal of the sciatic nerve.

stIntro: Although it is prohibited for Jews to eat the sciatic nerve,

summary: Eating a kezayis of the gid hanasheh gets forty lashes; eating a whole one, even if smaller, also gets lashes. The Sages and Rabbi Yehudah argue about eating from both legs.

chunks.en: Someone who eats a kezayis of the gid hanasheh
chunks.st: One who eats an olive-bulk of the sciatic nerve

chunks.en: gets forty lashes.
chunks.st: incurs forty lashes.

chunks.en: If he ate a whole one and it is not a kezayis,
chunks.st: If one eats an entire sciatic nerve and it does not constitute an olive-bulk, he is nevertheless

chunks.he: חַיָּב. אָכַל מִזֶּה כַזַּיִת וּמִזֶּה כַזַּיִת,
chunks.en: he is liable. If he ate a kezayis from this one and a kezayis from that one,
chunks.st: liable to receive lashes, because a complete sciatic nerve is a complete entity. If one ate an olive-bulk from this sciatic nerve in the right leg, and an olive-bulk from that sciatic nerve in the left leg,

chunks.en: he gets eighty lashes.
chunks.st: he incurs [sofeg] eighty lashes.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: He gets only forty.
chunks.st: He incurs only forty lashes,
chunks.stMore: for eating the olive-bulk from the right leg, and he is exempt for eating the olive-bulk from the left leg.

summary: If a thigh was cooked with the gid hanasheh in it, the thigh is forbidden only if the gid gave it a taste. We measure as if it were meat cooked with a turnip.

chunks.en: A thigh that was cooked with the gid hanasheh in it:
chunks.st: In the case of a thigh that was cooked with the sciatic nerve in it,

chunks.en: if there is enough to give a taste,
chunks.st: if there is enough of the sciatic nerve in it to impart its flavor to the thigh, the entire thigh

chunks.en: it is forbidden.
chunks.st: is forbidden for consumption.

chunks.en: How do we measure it?
chunks.st: How does one measure whether there is enough sciatic nerve to impart flavor to the meat of the entire thigh? One relates to it

chunks.en: Like meat with a turnip.
chunks.st: as though the sciatic nerve were meat imparting flavor to a turnip.
chunks.stMore: If meat the volume of the sciatic nerve would impart flavor to a turnip the volume of the thigh when they were cooked together, then the entire thigh is forbidden.

summary: If the gid hanasheh, or a piece of forbidden meat or fish, was cooked with other pieces and we can find it, the rest is forbidden only if it gave a taste. If we cannot find it, all the pieces are forbidden.

chunks.en: A gid hanasheh that was cooked with other sinews:
chunks.st: With regard to a sciatic nerve that was cooked with other sinews,

chunks.en: when he recognizes it,
chunks.st: when one identifies the sciatic nerve and removes it, the other sinews are forbidden if the sciatic nerve was large enough to

chunks.en: it depends on whether it gave a taste.
chunks.st: impart flavor.

chunks.en: But if not,
chunks.st: And if he does not identify it,

chunks.en: they are all forbidden.
chunks.st: all the sinews are forbidden
chunks.stMore: because each one could be the sciatic nerve;

chunks.en: And the gravy depends on whether it gave a taste.
chunks.st: but the broth is forbidden only if the sciatic nerve imparts flavor to the broth.

chunks.en: And also a piece of neveilah,
chunks.st: And similarly, in the case of a piece of an animal carcass

chunks.en: and also a piece of non-kosher fish,
chunks.st: or a piece of non-kosher fish

chunks.en: that were cooked with the other pieces:
chunks.st: that was cooked with similar pieces of kosher meat or fish,

chunks.en: when he recognizes them,
chunks.st: when one identifies the forbidden piece and removes it, the rest of the meat or fish is forbidden only if the forbidden piece was large enough to

chunks.en: it depends on whether it gave a taste.
chunks.st: impart flavor to the entire mixture.

chunks.en: But if not,
chunks.st: And if he does not identify and remove the forbidden piece,

chunks.en: they are all forbidden.
chunks.st: all the pieces are forbidden, due to the possibility that each piece one selects might be the forbidden piece;

chunks.en: And the gravy depends on whether it gave a taste.
chunks.st: but the broth is forbidden only if the forbidden piece imparts flavor to the broth.

summary: The gid hanasheh is forbidden only in kosher animals. Rabbi Yehudah says it was forbidden from the time of Yaakov's sons, before non-kosher animals were forbidden, but the Sages say it was given at Sinai.

chunks.en: It applies to a kosher animal,
chunks.st: The prohibition of eating the sciatic nerve applies to a kosher animal

chunks.en: and does not apply to a non-kosher animal.
chunks.st: and does not apply to a non-kosher animal.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: Even to a non-kosher animal.
chunks.st: It applies even to a non-kosher animal.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah said:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda said in explanation:

chunks.he: וַהֲלֹא מִבְּנֵי יַעֲקֹב נֶאֱסַר גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה,
chunks.en: Wasn't the gid hanasheh forbidden from the time of Yaakov's sons,
chunks.st: Wasn’t the sciatic nerve forbidden for the children of Jacob,
chunks.stMore: as it is written: “Therefore the children of Israel eat not the sciatic nerve” (Genesis 32:33),

chunks.en: when non-kosher animals were still allowed to them?
chunks.st: yet the meat of a non-kosher animal was still permitted to them?
chunks.stMore: Since the sciatic nerve of non-kosher animals became forbidden at that time, it remains forbidden now. The Rabbis

chunks.en: They said to him:
chunks.st: said to Rabbi Yehuda: The prohibition

chunks.en: It was said at Sinai,
chunks.st: was stated in Sinai,

chunks.en: but it was written in its place.
chunks.explain: In the story of Yaakov, where the Torah tells why.
